s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of hip pain and difficulty walking in an elderly patient with a history of osteoporosis treatment and previous hip surgery
salient_findings: Incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck
key_facts: 76-year-old woman
One week of right hip pain
Difficulty walking
Received denosumab for osteoporosis for five years
Underwent total hip arthroplasty for a left femoral neck fracture two years earlier
JOA score was 96 on the right and 76 on the left
Initial plain radiographs were reportedly normal
Repeat radiographs demonstrated an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck
Computed tomography confirmed a lateral cortical fracture without comminution
T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a high-signal bend in the same region
Bone mineral density was 0.840 g/cm2 in the lumbar spine and 0.899 g/cm2 in the right femoral neck
Laboratory studies revealed abnormal calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase, tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase-5b, type I procollagen N-terminal propeptide, and osteocalcin levels

shortlist.label: Atypical femoral fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of denosumab treatment and presents with an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck

shortlist.label: Osteoporotic fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of osteoporosis treatment and low bone mineral density

shortlist.label: Stress fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with acute onset of hip pain and difficulty walking

shortlist.label: Denosumab-related fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of denosumab treatment and presents with a fracture

shortlist.label: Insufficiency fracture
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has low bone mineral density and presents with a fracture

raw.rationale: The patient's history of long-term denosumab use, the presence of an incomplete transverse fracture in the lateral cortex of the right femoral neck without comminution, and the high-signal bend on T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging are consistent with an atypical femoral fracture

rejected.label: Osteoporotic fracture
rejected.why: While the patient has osteoporosis, the specific characteristics of the fracture, such as its location and lack of comminution, are more suggestive of an atypical femoral fracture

rejected.label: Stress fracture
rejected.why: Stress fractures typically occur in younger, more active individuals and are not as strongly associated with denosumab use

rejected.label: Denosumab-related fracture
rejected.why: While denosumab is a risk factor for atypical femoral fractures, 'denosumab-related fracture' is not a specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Insufficiency fracture
rejected.why: Insufficiency fractures typically occur in areas of weakened bone, often due to osteoporosis, but the specific characteristics of this fracture are more consistent with an atypical femoral fracture
